title: Lupin Ltd - 500257 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lupin Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR 7,827 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 25.1% (from 31.3%) as US Tolvaptan competition intensified.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 11% YoY to INR 7,827 crore, with India (+14.7%), Other Developed Markets (+46%) and API (+20%) offsetting a 9.3% YoY rise in the US and a 4% decline in Emerging Markets. US sales were USD 317 million, down 13.4% QoQ in constant currency, driven by Tolvaptan price erosion and Mirabegron LoE. EBITDA excluding forex and other income was INR 1,957 crore at a 25.1% margin, and management said margins will moderate in coming quarters. Management maintained FY27 US revenue guidance of USD 1.1-1.2 billion and EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25%.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales USD 317 million in Q2, down 13.4% QoQ cc on Tolvaptan price erosion (two new generic entrants; Lupin had ~50% share as sole generic) and Mirabegron LoE; H1 US sales about USD 683 million. FY27 guidance USD 1.1-1.2 billion maintained.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Grew 14.7% YoY vs IPM 14.7% in Q2; H1 prescription business +14.4% vs IPM 14.3%. Chronic segment +19.5% in H1 (66% of portfolio). Diabetes grew 25%+ in Q2, respiratory slowed sharply, cardiac slowed. Lupin's H1 outperformance was about 1.1x IPM vs its 1.2-1.3x target.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets (Europe, Canada, Australia)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,182 crore, +46% YoY, 15% of total revenue (11% in FY26); Europe +45% YoY. Licensed Yuvezzi (presbyopia eye drop) in Europe from Tenpoint Therapeutics; VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Declined 4% YoY on lower Brazil sales from Dapagliflozin competition, offset by double-digit growth in South Africa, Philippines and Mexico.

guidance_outlook: FY27 US revenue guidance maintained at USD 1.1-1.2 billion; management said Q1 and Q2 were above plan and will hold guidance to see if upside emerges.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of around 24-25% retained, with management acknowledging margins are likely to moderate in coming quarters.
FY27 R&D expected around 8% of sales; ETR expected 27-28% for the full year.
H2 FY27 organic growth expected around 20% excluding US.
FY28 US revenue expected to stay at USD 1 billion plus, supported by Apixaban, Dalbavancin, Pegfilgrastim and other biosimilars.
India formulations expected to grow 1.2-1.3x IPM; management said 2029-30 company EBITDA margin could return to 29-30% as specialty, 505(b)(2) and biosimilars scale, with FY28 a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin held up when Tolvaptan and Mirabegron revenue has fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is mainly Tolvaptan; mix shifts and forex tailwinds from Q1 forwards (set around INR 89-90) supported Q2 gross margin, which fell QoQ but less steeply than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan exit share and how many more entrants are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lupin held about 50% share as sole generic in recent months; a couple more entrants are possible. Management expects pricing pressure to cut margin and revenue contribution significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Will Apixaban need investment before launch, and can it hold share after generics arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, extra commercial investment is planned over the next couple of quarters for market access and channel relationships. Management expects some share retention in liquid-dosage segments and a longer window than exclusive generics.

qa_highlights.question: What drives India growth acceleration in H2 given H1 at about 1.1x IPM?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Gupta said H1 was 16% ahead of market but short of the 20-30% target; respiratory inhaler slowdown is expected to ease in H2, and cardiac should recover.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 US revenue match FY27 and does it include Apixaban?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US revenue should stay at USD 1 billion plus, which includes Apixaban; Tolvaptan pressure is offset by Apixaban, Dalbavancin and Pegfilgrastim.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 29-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said 29-30% is possible by FY29-30 as 505(b)(2), biosimilar and specialty products scale, with FY28 a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital deployment capacity for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would keep debt within twice EBITDA, about INR 16,000-17,000 crore of debt capacity plus INR 3,000-4,000 crore of balance-sheet cash, so up to about INR 20,000 crore. Priorities are specialty in Europe and US, and India at an appropriate cost.

risks_watch: Tolvaptan pricing erosion and further generic entrants; Mirabegron competition after September 2027.
Margin trajectory: Q2 EBITDA margin 25.1% against 24-25% full-year guidance implies a weaker H2; H2 operating expenses (field force, R&D, IT/AI) are rising.
India respiratory and cardiac slowdown; H1 growth at about 1.1x IPM vs 1.2-1.3x target.
Apixaban launch in Q1 FY28 depends on market access for a 505(b)(2) product; generics expected about 10 months after launch.
Brazil and emerging markets weakness from Dapagliflozin competition.
Forex tailwind from Q1 forwards may reverse; Middle East input cost pressure.
Pithampur Unit II remediation status; regulatory queries on Dulera and Diazepam nasal spray.
Respiratory filing timelines (Breo may slip into Q1 FY28).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term pipeline and India, but cautious on near term: management repeatedly said margins will moderate and FY28 is a year of investment and consolidation. Answers on Tolvaptan pricing and India H1 underperformance were direct, while questions on Apixaban share and biosimilar pricing got more general answers.
capex_capacity: Management said it is on track to file more than 15 US products in FY27 and expects to launch more than 60 US products over the next three years, including about 25 injectable and respiratory products, 5 biosimilars and 2-3 505(b)(2) products.
Pithampur Unit II: responses submitted and remediation on track; first green propellant MDI approved in India in the week before the call.

Respiratory filings: Spiriva Respimat exhibit batches done and filing planned this fiscal year; Breo (Ellipta) filing expected later this fiscal year, may slip a couple of months into Q1 FY28; seven to eight respiratory products targeted for filing within FY27 or shortly after.

Apixaban Oral Suspension (505(b)(2)): tentative approval received in Q2; launch planned in Q1 FY28; extra commercial investment planned over the next couple of quarters for market access and channel relationships; Somerset site is the filing site and management said capacity is sufficient for the upside scenario.

Capital deployment: debt capacity framed at twice EBITDA, about INR 16,000-17,000 crore, plus about INR 3,000-4,000 crore of balance-sheet cash, so up to about INR 20,000 crore; priorities are specialty in Europe and US, and India acquisitions at an appropriate cost.

Opex: Q2 cost increase tied to field force expansion, settlement-related Mirabegron licence fees (expected to reverse), and IT, platform and AI investment over the next few quarters; R&D guided to about 8% of sales for FY27 with possible optimisation of non-priority lines in FY28.
demand_pricing: US Q2 sales USD 317 million, down 13.4% QoQ in constant currency, on Tolvaptan price erosion after two new generic entrants and Mirabegron LoE; partly offset by seasonal and volume gains. H1 US sales about USD 683 million.

Tolvaptan: Lupin held about 50% share in recent months as sole generic; a couple more entrants are possible. Management expects pricing, not share, to drive a significant cut in margin and revenue contribution.
FY27 US guidance of USD 1.1-1.2 billion maintained; management said Q1 and Q2 were above plan and will hold guidance to see if upside emerges.

FY28 US revenue expected at USD 1 billion plus, with Apixaban, Dalbavancin and Pegfilgrastim as offsets to Tolvaptan pressure; Mirabegron competition expected after September 2027. FY29 seen as a growth year.

India: Q2 growth 14.7% vs IPM 14.7%; core prescription +13.8% with 6% volume. H1 prescription +14.4% vs IPM 14.3%; chronic +19.5% in H1 vs IPM 17.2%; chronic share about 66%, target 70% over five years. Diabetes 25%+ in Q2; respiratory (inhaler) and cardiac slowed. H1 about 1.1x IPM vs 1.2-1.3x target; management said H1 was 16% ahead of market.
Other Developed Markets: INR 1,182 crore, +46% YoY, 15% of revenue; Europe +45% YoY. Yuvezzi (presbyopia) licensed from Tenpoint for Europe; VISUfarma acquisition closed.
Emerging Markets down 4% YoY on lower Brazil sales from Dapagliflozin competition; double-digit growth in South Africa, Philippines and Mexico.

Apixaban oral suspension: addressable brand market USD 10-plus billion; management expects margin similar to an exclusive product with commercial investment; generic entry about 10 months after launch.

Pricing: management said biosimilar pricing erosion and discounting help less than in small-molecule generics; Pegfilgrastim launched via partner Valorum. Gross margin 74.2% vs 74.6% in Q1, helped by Q1 forward-contract FX drag reversing (forwards set around INR 89-90).
Company EBITDA margin: FY27 guidance 24-25% retained; 29-30% possible by FY29-30 as 505(b)(2), biosimilars and specialty scale; FY28 a consolidation year.
key_quotes: As anticipated, competition in Tolvaptan intensified with the entry of two additional generic players.
We expect competitive intensity in Tolvaptan to increase further, with the possibility of additional entrants over the coming quarters.
For H1, we are 16% ahead of the market, but definitely not where we need to be.

Yes, we are planning to make additional investments in the next couple of quarters to be able to get the right market access and channel expertise and relationships to be able to build share in the exclusive window that we have prior to the generics coming in.
